items.title: This image tells the story of a climate catastrophe
items.description: Stefan Rahmstorf was holidaying in southern France when he came face to face with the climate future he has tried to fight.

items.title: 'People are really suffering': Ukraine's drones bring war home to Russia
items.description: For years, people in Russia's largest and most affluent cities were shielded from the impacts of their country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but not anymore.

items.title: 'What's happened to me?': Bearing witness as my nan faced dementia
items.description: The woman who once chased down a donkey to save her granddaughter would one day need saving herself — and teach me a lesson about love.

items.title: Live: Aussies sweep women's mile after sprinters' history-making triumph
items.description: Australia's stuns the field to claim gold in the men's 4x100m relay for the first time since 1974, as Abbey Caldwell leads an all-Australian podium on a record-breaking final day of athletics action. Follow live.

items.title: Pure shock as Diamonds fumble Australia's most anticipated gold medal
items.description: The Diamonds will miss the Commonwealth Games gold medal match for the first time after a shock semifinal loss to Jamaica in front of a Hydro crowd baying for Australia's downfall.

items.title: Trump's new respect for Zelenskyy highlights Netanyahu's problem
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy must have felt a little triggered when he walked into the Oval Office this week. But Trump's public anger is now often directed at another at-war ally.

items.title: Family of young mother who died after missed UTI speak out
items.description: Gia Lam gave birth to her son and was dead three days later. A coronial inquest found her death was preventable. Her family are now breaking their silence.

items.title: Voters are starting to ask a new question about politics, money
items.description: Debate about money in politics has traditionally revolved around whether politicians have broken the rules. But voters are increasingly asking what good judgement looks like.

items.title: Prices to jump at the bowser as fuel excise cut ends tonight
items.description: The price of unleaded and diesel will climb in the next week as the government's fuel excise cut officially ends. But experts say prices won't go as high as they did due to increased supply.

items.title: How people are looking outside the box to combat crippling housing crisis
items.description: From Tasmania to Broken Hill and the Northern Rivers of NSW, people are finding ways to beat the housing crisis.

items.title: H5 bird flu testing underway for mass mortality of terns on SA island
items.description: South Australian authorities are investigating a mass bird mortality event after more than 80 dead and sick birds were found off the state's south-east coast.

items.title: Spain slams 'selfish' EU, sets up floating barriers
items.description: European Union states are demanding stricter international border controls and have called an emergency meeting as Spain reassures safety of Schengen Area.

items.title: 'We're blowing this thing into the harbour': 50 years since woodchip bombing
items.description: A stolen car full of explosives, a hostage held at gunpoint, and a plan gone awry. Inside the anti-woodchip bombing at WA's Bunbury port in 1976.

items.title: 'We are not a monoculture and never have been,' Penny Wong tells Garma Festival
items.description: On the second day of Garma Festival, Foreign Minister Penny Wong emphasised the strategic importance of ties between First Nations peoples and Australia's Pacific neighbours.

items.title: Queens of the Stone Age's Josh Homme on health, honesty and evolution
items.description: Have Queens Of The Stone Age mellowed? After 30 years the rock titans are finding "new ways to do old things".

items.title: 'Wannabe' a music quiz legend? Right this way...
items.description: Hey ya! It's your time to shine with the Spicks and Specks quiz.

items.title: 'Who says girls can't play baseball?': America's pastime goes pro for women
items.description: Baseball is 'America's pastime', but women have not been able to play professionally for decades. That has now changed with the inaugural Women's Pro Baseball League underway.

items.title: Victoria's tobacco kingpin is in jail, but violence still grips the state
items.description: Kazem Hamad, once dubbed one of the most dangerous wanted men in the world, is now behind bars. But the violence on Victorian streets has continued unabated.

items.title: Australia's gamble on quantum computing in the age of AI
items.description: More than half a century after the first computers were built, Australia is aiming to be a global innovator in quantum computing. But can it compete with the rise of AI?

items.title: China's 'push towards assimilation' could drive its minorities to extinction
items.description: China's new ethnic unity law is threatening to make the languages and culture of 55 different ethnic groups extinct.

items.title: Russian missile attacks on Kyiv kill at least ten and injure dozens
items.description: Ukraine downed only one of 27 Russian ballistic missiles during the attack as the country lacks interceptors for the US Patriot systems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

items.title: Sandstone miner scraps Lockyer Valley project after farmers' pleas
items.description: A quiet farming community found itself at the centre of a major battle when mining threatened their land. What happened next surprised everyone.

items.title: Famed mountaineer Nirmal Purja confirmed dead in Pakistan avalanche
items.description: The Netflix-famous climber died, among nine others, climbing the world's 12th highest mountain.

items.title: A small Australian town's surprising link to The Wizard of Oz
items.description: The town of Kaniva, and even the smaller settlement of Lillimur, in far-western Victoria, played an important role in the astonishing success of the legendary Hollywood movie, The Wizard of Oz.

items.title: James Cook University students fight to save study week
items.description: Students are hopeful they can overturn a university's controversial decision to scrap study vacation week before exams.
